function: Joint transmit and receive beamforming design for bistatic ISAC (information beams, sensing covariance, receive beams) minimizing the target-position CRB under communication rate constraints (p. 1, p. 7).
system: Bistatic ISAC, 8-antenna transmit BS and 8-antenna receive BS, 4 single-antenna downlink users, 3 uplink users, 4 targets; no RIS; Rician fading; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 10).
method: ISACNet: complex fully connected pre-processing, multi-head self- and cross-attention encoder (3 iterations, 20 heads), model-based decoder; unsupervised training with penalty loss, no labels (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: Own simulator: random user and target locations, Rician fading (factor 3), path-loss exponent 3.5; 90,000 training and 10,000 test samples, test labels from the SCA algorithm (p. 10).
test_conditions: Trained at Pmax 8 W and Rician factor 3; tested at Pmax 6, 8, 10 W and Rician factor 1, 3, 5; no other change reported (p. 12).
baselines: Non-learned: own SCA algorithm (reference for ISACNet); MMSE design [37] (versus SCA design). Learned: complex MLP, vanilla CNN [23], shuffle-attention CNN [28] (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Effectiveness (ratio of SCA CRB to method CRB), feasibility rate, inference time; CRB versus downlink and uplink rate requirements (pp. 10-11).
complexity: Measured average inference time: ISACNet 3.71 ms versus SCA 13.97 s (Table I, p. 11); no FLOPs or parameter count.
q1_support: p. 10: "the Rician fading [36] is adopted for the small-scale fading with the Rician factor κ being 3". Custom simulator with its own path-loss model; no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned anywhere.
q2_support: p. 12: "The ISACNet is trained at a transmit power budget of Pmax = 8 W and a Rician factor of κ = 3", then tested at Pmax 6, 8, 10 W and κ 1, 3, 5 (Table II), so κ = 1 and 5 were not used in training.
q3_support: p. 11: "in comparison with the proposed SCA-based algorithm, a CMLP-based approach" and "two CNN baselines, i.e., vanilla CNN [23] and Shuffle-Attention (SA) CNN [28]"; Table I (p. 11) compares effectiveness and feasibility rate of all of them.
q4_support: p. 11: "Inference time: The average running time required to calculate the solution on the test set"; Table I gives 3.71 ms for ISACNet and 13.97 s for SCA. No FLOPs or parameter counts are given.
q5_support: p. 10: "By performing multiple Monte Carlo realizations of the locations of DUEs, UUEs, and targets and the Rician fading, we generate the training set". Own simulated data; no code or data link and no public dataset in the paper.
notes: Included on ISACNet, the learned part. The paper also proposes a classical SCA algorithm (p. 6-7), which is the non-learned reference. Area 5 rather than 3: the beamformers and the sensing covariance serve sensing and communication (p. 1, p. 5 problem P1). The CRB concerns target positions, but the learned model only outputs beamformers and does not estimate positions. q2 is borderline: a change of Rician factor and power budget between training and test (p. 12); the paper says κ = 1 needs re-training or fine-tuning. q3: the MMSE design [37] is compared only with the SCA design (p. 10, Figs. 4-5); ISACNet is compared with SCA and with the learned CMLP, CNN [23] and SA-CNN [28] in Table I (p. 11).
